findings.rationale: Accepted: the generation-2 repair added the prefix-open rule but left the older out-of-scope sentence standing beside it, so the two read as mutually exclusive. The stale sentence is deleted; the section 3a match row is now the only statement of guard scope.

Accepted, and a real silent-no-op: on the full-id path the mapper is bypassed, so --cursor-fast would be parsed and ignored. It is now a die_precondition to pass --cursor-fast with a full --model id, with the message telling the caller to pass the -fast id directly.

Accepted: the wrappers had no stated MODEL contract while the argv always passed --model. Frozen: both wrappers require an explicit full model id for --runner cursor, with no cursor default and no alias resolution (the mapper and --cursor-fast stay dispatch-hetero-only); a missing or alias --model is a die_precondition, and both acceptance commands carry --model.

Accepted: a bare enum widening cannot express implementer-only, because the tuple validation is shared. Section 3b now carries an explicit admission matrix and Phase 3 specifies a role-aware guard - cursor accepted for the implementer role, rejected for every reviewer-class role and for dual occupancy - each with a negative test.

Accepted: the six schema enum sites are what make cursor a routable review-loop role rather than a base-dispatch receipt field, so validating them in Phase 2 left that phase contract-inconsistent - a roster the schema accepts and no wrapper can run. The enum moves to Phase 3; Phase 2 keeps only the readiness maps.

Accepted and closed with a receipt rather than a promise: --list-models was load-bearing in Global Constraint 5, Phase 1, and the Phase 5 receipt list, yet had no probe row. Now P14 - rc 0, 208 stdout lines, stderr empty, header plus blank plus 204 entries of the form <id> - <display name> - with the parser specified against that observed shape.

Accepted, independently reached and correctly framed as a violation of this plan's own thesis: an unverified flag was carrying the stale-table guarantee. P14 records the probe and its output shape, and the Phase 1 parser and Phase 5 receipt check are specified against it.

Accepted, and the single sharpest finding of the round. Containment is genuinely unsound here and the probe proves it: in the real P14 output, grep -c 'cursor-grok-4.6-low' returns 2 while the anchored form returns 1, so a removed non-fast id would validate against its own -fast variant and the fail-closed guarantee would be void. The check is now parse-into-a-set plus string equality, recorded as hazard P15, with a Phase 1 acceptance case that stubs an inventory missing the non-fast id but retaining the fast one and requires it to fail.

Accepted, and it caught the plan violating the very rule it invokes: Phase 3 admitted cursor to the implementer roster two phases before Stage 1 ran, so a rail that failed or never ran qualification would have remained assignable. Admission moves to Phase 5 and is conditional on the recorded outcome - the entry exists iff the outcome is a pass. Two ordered rules are now stated: admission must not precede executability, and admission must not precede qualification.
